system.summary: Numbered code of 1,592 elements, Weber's WE025 (Weber 1979, pp. 470-480): common words as single groups, longer words spelled from syllable groups; a circle or diamond over a group adds -s.
system.sibling_key: Poinsett to Monroe, Buenos Aires 14 June 1814 (catalogue 651; M37 roll 2 frame 0098, Duplicate 0100), same code with a clerk's interlinear decode, printed by Manning 1925 vol. 1 doc. 201.
system.notes: Identified as WE025 on 11 Nov 2026 (beling/README.md). 1315, written where 'a' is wanted three times in the 1814 letter, is 'hu' in Weber (not explained); 1215 = a. Cross and caret read from use only: the cross doubles a letter, the caret adds -ed.

prior_solution.where: 1813: Manning 1925 vol. 2 doc. 442 prints the cipher places as '(undeciphered cipher)'; no decipherment found. 1814 (catalogue 651): the clerk's interlinear decode on the RC, printed in Manning 1925 vol. 1 doc. 201 (found 27 Oct 2026). The code table: Weber 1979 prints WE025 in full (pp. 470-480); no reading of the 1813 letter with it found (Weber, this repository, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana, Manning; searched 11 Nov 2026).

solution.what: Manning vol. 2 doc. 442 read for the clear context; web search for a decipherment or the 1810 cypher: none found.
Fetched M37 roll 2 frames 0091-0102 from the NARA catalogue; the letter is at 0092-0094.
Transcribed passages P1-P9 (437 groups, 256 distinct) line by line; P0 on frame 0092 illegible after background flattening.
Applied the repo's US code tables (JQA/Department 1803-40, Armstrong THE=972, Pinckney, 1788 legation, Jefferson 1787, Mountflorence 1801) directly: noise.
shift_test.py: every constant shift and mod 1600/1700 of the same tables, scored with lang en-modern 4-gram; best z 4.3 among about 9,000 settings, junk decodes.
Sumter, Rio 1813 (M121 vol. 1A frames 0035-0039, interlinear decode) checked: the = 798, of = 1399; a different code.
Poinsett 14 June 1814 (frame 0098, duplicate 0100) found in the same code with a clerk's interlinear decode; 88 values aligned into key_1814.tsv.
decode.py applied the sibling key to the 1813 groups: 158 of 437 have a value; fragments, no sentence reads yet.

Context pass over the 1813 decode: only 'Lima' (249 413, twice in the Lima paragraph) cross-checks sibling syllables; no new values, the other unknown groups occur once or twice in contexts that do not fix them.
Weber 1979 not online; the HSP calendar of the Poinsett papers (1941, HathiTrust full view) is behind a bot check and was not searched.
Lowry, La Guaira 1810-12, held a cypher for the 1810 agents (Manning); M84 roll 1 frames 0014-0090 viewed: no code; M37 roll 1 (Shaler) has no code frames.
Catalogue 651, 14 June 1814: RC (0097-0098) and Duplicate (0099-0100) transcribed line by line with the clerk's glosses; merged text 123 groups, 90 distinct (ciphertext_1814.txt).
Manning vol. 1 (1925) doc. 201, pp. 335-336 prints the 14 June 1814 letter with both code passages in clear: the clerk's decode word for word. Catalogue 651 was already deciphered.

Clerk's decode checked group by group against both copies and Manning: 122 of 123 groups carry a value; key corrections 964 principle, 1236 it, 1087 two, 737 between, 1179 ct / 765 ion, 480 t; group 39 unglossed.
decode.py re-run on the 1813 letter with the corrected key: 161 of 437 groups have a value (was 158); still fragments.
Manning vols. 1-2 searched for other Poinsett letters with code: none decoded besides 14 June 1814.

Beling contribution: the numerals of P1-P9 transcribed afresh from frames 0093-0094 and frozen (sha256 d31b3043...) before WE025 was tried; doubtful digits kept open as {a|b}; not blind (the repo decode had been seen). Against transcription.tsv: 425 of 437 groups agree (420 first readings, 5 second), 5 differ, 7 have an unread digit in one or both (beling/transcription/, beling/decryption_1813-02-20.txt).

Beling contribution: code 1355 identified as WE025, printed in full by Weber 1979, pp. 470-480 (1,592 elements). Table transcribed from the book's text layer, 16 places checked on the page images, frozen by sha256 at 2026-11-11T10:37:23Z before any decoding; one correction after the freeze (668 fect). Against key_1814.tsv, 27 values differ: 21 syllable splits, 462/1495 dra-w with 39 = should, 618 iu, 337/435 transcription errors (338 never, 485 dom), 1315 = hu not explained.

Beling contribution: 14 June 1814 decoded with WE025 alone and compared with the clerk's decipherment: 0.935 of letters matched (376 of 401); 200 shuffled keys mean 0.184, best 0.306, z 16.3; 0.954 with the two image rereads. Not blind: the agent had seen the clerk's values; no threshold declared (beling/tests/heldout_1814_result.txt).

Beling contribution: 20 Feb 1813 decoded with WE025 from the frozen numerals: 406 of 437 groups read as frozen (92.9%), 4 after an image reread, 20 on an assumed digit misread (not confirmed), 7 holes; all nine passages P1-P9 join Manning's clear text; P0 still illegible. Read in part, read_share 0.916 (beling/reading_1813-02-20.md).

Beling contribution: prior art for a tie between Poinsett's code and WE025 searched in Weber 1979, this repository (files, open and closed pull requests and issues, commits of 9-11 Nov 2026), Tomokiyo's Cryptiana and Manning 1925. Nothing found.

texts.label: Poinsett to Monroe, Santiago, 20 Feb 1813, M37 roll 2 frames 0092-0094 (catalogue 639), read with WE025
texts.summary: Writing from Santiago while the Carreras governed Chile and Lima's cruisers blockaded Valparaiso and Conception (Manning's clear text), Poinsett reports in code that he has taken a part in the revolution beyond his instructions, that a small naval force with five thousand stand of arms would insure the fall of Lima, that his journey to Arauco is really to leave the militia in patriot hands before independence is declared, and that the new governor of the bishopric, proposed by him, is at his disposal.
texts.note: Contributed by Andrew Beling with AI agents (beling/README.md). read_share is the repo measure on the reading, Manning's clear words before each passage included; 406 of 437 groups (92.9%) read as frozen. The decryption is laid out against Daniel Bourdeau's transcription.tsv; the reading uses our own frozen transcription (beling/transcription/). P0 (frame 0092) not read.

reading_review.by: Andrew Beling, with two independent AI-agent readings (Claude)
reading_review.note: Read as sentences, 12 Nov 2026. P1-P9 build coherent English throughout; the holes (five unexplained groups and about twenty marked guesses) are scattered, and every sentence still parses. P0 on frame 0092 is not legible and stays unread, hence read in part. Marking fixed on review: two supplied words and two reread groups now marked.
